Where it began

Mohammed Siraj was born in Secunderabad on 13 March 1994. He came to serious cricket late. He first bowled at 16, and with a tennis ball rather than a hard one, and he was 19 before he played club cricket at all. He made up for lost time quickly: in his very first match he took nine wickets.

He made his first-class debut for Hyderabad in November 2015, and in the 2016–17 Ranji Trophy he was his side's leading wicket-taker, with 41 wickets at 18.92.

The player

His first international outing was a Twenty20 match against New Zealand in November 2017, and his first wicket was Kane Williamson, which is a fine way to open the account. His Test debut followed on 26 December 2020 in Australia, where Marnus Labuschagne became his first Test victim. By the fourth Test of that same series he had his first five-wicket haul.

By October 2026 he had played 48 Tests and taken 144 wickets at 29.63, with five five-wicket innings and a best of 6 for 15. In the 2025 series in England for the new Anderson–Tendulkar Trophy he took 23 wickets, more than anyone else on either side, and was player of the match in the fifth Test.

What made him special

He bowled with energy that never seemed to run out, and he saved some of his best days for the biggest occasions. In the 2023 Asia Cup final against Sri Lanka he took 6 for 21, became the first Indian to take four wickets in a single over and was named player of the match. Early that year he had also risen to the top of the world rankings for one-day bowlers.

Batting was another matter. His 192 Test runs came at 5.05, with a top score of 22. Yet he was not out 27 times, so whatever else bowlers said about him, they could not always get rid of him.

Away from the middle

Wisden named him one of its Cricketers of the Year in its 2026 almanack. He was part of the India squads that won the Twenty20 World Cup in 2024 and again in 2026. In the Indian Premier League he played for Sunrisers Hyderabad, Royal Challengers Bangalore and Gujarat Titans, and in 2020 he became the first bowler in the league to send down two maiden overs in a row in one match. In July 2025 he opened a restaurant, Joharfa, in Banjara Hills in his home city.

And finally

Not many Test fast bowlers can say they started out with a tennis ball at 16. Siraj made the hard ball look as though he had been bowling it all his life.
